presentation.label: GYRE
presentation.summary: A loop you hold that keeps spiralling: two grains half a window apart make it unity-gain, so Decay at 0 holds for ever and Rise climbs or sinks it each pass.
presentation.overview: A loop you hold that keeps spiralling: two grains half a window apart make it unity-gain, so Decay at 0 holds for ever and Rise climbs or sinks it each pass.

controls.name: Size
controls.doc: Loop length, ~40 ms to ~2.9 s, squared so the short end -- where it reads as a stutter rather than a phrase -- gets most of the travel. On knob 1: verbatim-stock LineSel handler, and the control you reach for first. Range 0–100.

controls.name: Feed
controls.doc: How much of what you play enters the loop. At 0 the loop is sealed and what is already captured is all there is; turn it up and the loop keeps absorbing. This is the record control. Range 0–100.

controls.name: Decay
controls.doc: 0 holds forever -- the loop neither grows nor fades, because the two-grain window sums to exactly 1. Above 0 it fades, squared so the bottom of the knob is a very slow bloom and the top a short tail. This is the way out, and it always works. Range 0–100.

controls.name: Rise
controls.doc: Per-pass pitch ratio: 0 is an octave down, 50 unity, 100 an octave up. The shift COMPOUNDS around the loop, so the held audio climbs or sinks endlessly instead of sitting still. Range 0–100.

controls.name: Glide
controls.doc: Depth of an onset-triggered ramp on that ratio. A new phrase resets the ramp, so the loop starts at pitch and drifts away over Span. Range 0–100.

controls.name: Span
controls.doc: How long the Glide ramp takes, ~0.19 s to ~8 s. Cubic in the knob so the long end keeps its resolution. Range 0–100.

controls.name: Tone
controls.doc: Low-pass inside the loop. This is what makes a held loop darken as it circulates rather than repeating identically forever. Range 0–100.

limitations: Hardware untested on the original MS-70CDR with OS 2.10.
